subject: Hosted API: Cold-prefix regeneration causing p95/p99 spikes
messages:
From: Diane Kelly <diane.kelly@helixhealth.com>

Date: 2026-08-04T01:12:00Z
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes since midnight deploy

Hi Lauren,

We're seeing a sharp increase in p95 and p99 latency on the Hosted API for our integration since around 00:30 UTC. Error rate has ticked up (5xx) and a few user-facing requests timed out. Our dashboards show a correlated jump in downstream token latency. This began right after your scheduled midnight push.

Is this something you can patch quickly? Our morning batch runs at 03:00 and this is blocking a few production jobs.

Attached: a short CSV with p95/p99 samples and a screenshot.

Thanks,
Diane

On 2026-08-04 01:28 UTC Lauren Bishop wrote:
> Hi Diane — sorry for the disruption. We're looking into it now. I've looped in SRE (Monica) and the runtime owner (Marcus).

Checked the first-pass telemetry. We're seeing a sharp increase in cold KV lookups and a simultaneous spike in tail latency on the hosted-inference cluster in us-west-2. Heap of calls are falling back to slower storage paths.

Hypothesis: a targeted TTL refresh/maintenance job kicked off during the deploy window and triggered a broad prefix invalidation (or churn) — that would explain global cold prefix regeneration and the p99 blowups.

I'm pulling KV invalidation traces and the prefix eviction logs now (attaching tail extracts). If confirmed, mitigation options:
- Roll back the maintenance toggle (if it's a canary flag).
- Enable transient warmup (pre-populate top prefixes).
- Apply a temporary routing rule to route HelixHealth to dedicated warmed pool.

Will update with logs in 10 minutes.

—Monica
Monica Patel
SRE, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: monica.patel@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-04T02:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes since midnight deploy

Good catch Monica — I can see the same in kernel-level traces: a TTL reconciliation job in the model catalog service sent a purge request that missed a safety window and pushed a full set of prefix tombstones to the serving layer. The serving runtime then attempted to regenerate many KV entries concurrently, causing KV backend saturation and stalled token-serving paths.

Immediate actions I pushed:
- Disabled the TTL reconciler job (rolled back the flag).
- Applied rate-limiting to prefix warmup tasks (throttle to 10/s per region).
- Bumped HelixHealth requests onto warm pool via routing override to reduce tail exposure.

I'm seeing tail latency start to degrade around 02:00 but not fully recovered. Keeping the warm override for HelixHealth for the next 4 hours and monitoring.

I'll draft a short RCA and mitigation plan; Monica to collect traces for postmortem.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin

Subject: Post-incident update and exec note — HelixHealth latency regression (INC-5123)

Team — putting a quick summary in the thread for execs and the customer. Leaving the live traces and the detailed postmortem draft in the linked doc.

Summary:
- Impact: HelixHealth observed p95/p99 latency regression and transient 5xx errors between ~00:30–02:30 UTC. Primary customer impact: delayed morning batch completion with retries.
- Root cause: unintended global prefix invalidation triggered by a TTL reconciliation job that ran during the deploy window. The invalidation caused mass KV cache regeneration and downstream backend saturation.
- Mitigations applied: TTL reconciler flag rolled back, warmup throttles added, HelixHealth routed to warmed pool, telemetry dashboards updated.
- Next steps:
  1) Finalize RCA and publish (Marcus/Monica) by EOD today.
  2) Add safety window gating for TTL reconciler jobs + deploy-time lockdown (Jonas).
  3) Add pre-warm plan for top ten customers and an automated soft fallback for routed warm pools (Product + Runtime).
  4) Offer HelixHealth a service credit and formal incident summary for their audit (Lauren — coordinate with finance).

Customer-facing note sent and they acknowledged the mitigation; they requested the full RCA for audit evidence. I'm tagging this INC-5123 and linking the draft: drive.redwood.com/incident/helix-20260804.

—Lauren
